sources.title: Macao SAR Public Security Police Force: Immigration Control
sources.publisher: Public Security Police Force, Macao Special Administrative Region
sources.officialityEvidence: The live gov.mo service identifies the Public Security Police Force as content provider and publishes its current immigration-control requirements, exemptions, entry-permit procedure and stay schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visitors from Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Vietnam are required to apply for a Macao visa in advance.

policies.title: Macao: EU/Schengen ordinary-passport 90-day visa and entry-permit exemption
policies.summary: The current Public Security Police schedule lists these EU/Schengen passport issuers in the 90-day visa-and-entry-permit-exempt cohort.
conditions: The ordinary-passport stay limit is a maximum of 90 days. It is a short-visit visa and entry-permit exemption, not a work, residence or special-document right.

A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay. Visitors need onward/return arrangements and means of subsistence as described by the PSP; entry remains subject to refusal grounds and individual immigration control.
The result excludes diplomatic/official/service passports, residence cards, transit, crew, extensions and nationality-plus-document exceptions.

policies.title: Macao: named ordinary-passport 90-day visa and entry-permit exemptions
policies.summary: The current Public Security Police schedule records these named ordinary-passport issuers in the separate 90-day exemption cohort.
conditions: The ordinary-passport stay limit is a maximum of 90 days. The PSP’s named-exemption list supports only visitor admission under this schedule.
A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay; onward/return arrangements, funds, admissibility and all entry-refusal grounds remain applicable.
It does not determine work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Macao: named ordinary-passport three-month visa and entry-permit exemptions
policies.summary: The Public Security Police stay schedule records these named passport issuers as exempt for a maximum of three months.
conditions: The stated ordinary-passport visitor limit is a maximum of three months. It does not establish work, residence, study, transit, crew or special-document rights.
A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay; onward/return arrangements, means and entry-refusal grounds remain applicable.
This grouping does not apply diplomatic, official, service, identity-card or residence-document routes to an ordinary passport code.

policies.title: Macao: Brunei and Kazakhstan ordinary-passport 14-day exemptions
policies.summary: The Public Security Police stay schedule records Brunei and Kazakhstan passports as exempt for a maximum of 14 days.
conditions: The stated ordinary-passport visitor limit is a maximum of 14 days, not a general 30- or 90-day entitlement.
A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay; onward/return arrangements, means, admissibility and entry-refusal grounds remain applicable.
It excludes work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/service and special-document conditions.

policies.title: Macao: British ordinary-passport six-month visa and entry-permit exemption
policies.summary: The Public Security Police schedule expressly gives British citizens holding a British passport a maximum six-month visa-and-entry-permit-exempt stay.
conditions: This classification is restricted to British citizens holding a British passport; it does not resolve other British statuses or documents.
The stated visitor limit is a maximum of six months. Passport validity, onward/return arrangements, funds, refusal grounds and individual immigration control still apply.
It excludes work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/service and special-document cases.

policies.title: Macao: named ordinary-passport 30-day visa and entry-permit exemptions
policies.summary: These named nationalities are in the Public Security Police’s current written-exemption list and fall under its otherwise-stated 30-day passport/travel-document visitor limit.
conditions: The schedule’s default maximum limit for holders of a valid passport or travel document is 30 days where no listed longer or shorter period applies.
The written exemption list excludes United States diplomatic passports; this ordinary-passport classification does not apply diplomatic/official/service documents.

A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay. Onward/return arrangements, means, entry-refusal grounds, employment, residence, transit, crew and individual-admissibility limitations are preserved.

policies.title: Macao: non-exempt ordinary passports eligible for border-issued Entry Permit
policies.summary: For these foreign ordinary passports, the current Public Security Police rule supplies an Entry Permit, expressly called visa-upon-arrival, at any border checkpoint; the six expressly advance-visa nationalities and document-specific China/Hong Kong/Macao cases are excluded.
conditions: The Entry Permit is an Authorization to Enter and Stay, explicitly described by the PSP as visa-upon-arrival, requested at any Border Control Department checkpoint. It is classified as visa on arrival, not eVisa or visa-free.

Once approved, the visitor Authorization to Stay is a maximum of 30 days; the current listed individual fee is MOP200 one-off or MOP300 multiple, with stated alternative fees for family passports, children and qualifying groups.

A passport must be valid at least 90 days beyond intended stay. Onward/return arrangements, means of subsistence, security/admissibility and entry-refusal grounds remain applicable; advance authorization or a Macao visa are alternative procedures, not a nationality-wide electronic route.

This policy excludes Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Vietnam, which the PSP expressly requires to obtain an advance Macao visa; it also does not flatten Mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao passport/document arrangements.

policies.title: Macao: six named ordinary passports requiring advance Macao visa
policies.summary: The current Public Security Police guidance expressly requires visitors from these six countries to obtain a Macao visa in advance through a Chinese embassy or consulate.
conditions: The advance visa is applied for through a Chinese embassy or consulate. The ordinary border Entry Permit route is not available to this named cohort.
The source does not establish an eVisa route, duration, fee, entry count or any work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/service or special-document exception for them.
Passport validity, onward/return arrangements, funds, security/admissibility and entry-refusal conditions still apply at actual entry.

conflicts.explanation: Argentina is in the current PSP written-exemption list and its passport is in the 30-day visa-and-entry-permit-exempt cohort.
Dominican Republic is not Dominica: it is absent from the PSP written exemption list and therefore uses the border Entry Permit route.
Fiji is expressly included in the current PSP written-exemption list and falls under the 30-day ordinary-passport limit.
The PSP does not list Taiwan in the written exemption cohort; its special Mainland Taiwan-permit rule is document-specific and does not alter the ordinary Taiwan-passport border Entry Permit route.

unresolved.reason: The PSP distinguishes Mainland Exit Permits, Taiwan-Resident permits and a PRC passport only for seven-day transit with a flight ticket and destination entry visa. It does not state a general ordinary-PRC-passport visitor route, so a document-specific rule is not flattened to this passport code.

The PSP gives one-year exemption to Hong Kong Permanent Identity Card or Re-entry Permit holders and a separate seven-day transit rule for HKSAR passports with flight ticket and destination entry visa. Neither proves a general ordinary-HKSAR-passport visitor status.

The current PSP page gives document-and-status-specific entry treatment for Macao permanent residents, Residence Authorization holders and special stay documents, but no direct statement normalizing a Macao ordinary passport alone as citizenship/right of entry. Citizenship is not inferred.
